title: A Team Workflow for Focused Changes
description: Explore standard industry branching workflows, master built-in help commands, apply core best practices, and review essential Git vocabulary.

blocks.content: A team needs predictable changes that reviewers can understand. A shared workflow turns individual commits into collaboration. What is the smallest Git action that keeps the work safe?

A workflow is the team agreement for how changes move from idea to release. Small focused commits make review, recovery, and collaboration easier.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Working files"] -->|"choose an action"| B["Git history"] -->|"share or recover"| C["Team project"]
```

blocks.question: Why prefer focused commits?
options: They are easier to review and recover
They remove the need for tests
blocks.explanation: A small commit tells one clear story, which makes later work safer.

blocks.prompt: Model the Git idea in a tiny simulator. Export a function named `commitFile` that takes `(working, staged, file)` and returns a new staged list containing `file` once. Do not change either input list.

tests.description: works when no working files are listed yet
keeps an already staged file while adding another
